clue.text: Unusual play with Act I very strange

indicators.note: very strange tells us the letters of the words that precede it are to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a play, especially its first act, bizarre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very strange' makes an anagram of PLAY plus ACT I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atypical departs from the norm, a straightforward synonym of unusual.

clue.text: That sari naturally covers a lady of some importance

indicators.note: the phrase That sari naturally covers, or holds within it, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A sari is the natural garment for a woman of standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' says the answer is held inside thaT SARI NAturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian emperor, certainly a woman of rank.

clue.text: Commits scales of charges for each domestic animal brought over

indicators.note: in a down clue, pieces brought over are set above the word mentioned earlier

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a pet is a domestic animal
rates are scales of charges, as levied by a council

explanation.surface: A vet's price list sets fees for every pet, and someone imports an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' puts PER and PET above RATES in this down entry, reversing their order in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime is to carry it out, so perpetrates is a synonym of commits.

clue.text: From small farm, creditor has nothing on paper

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A lender's claim on a smallholding comes to nothing in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Female bird I found in meadow

indicators.note: found in says the bird and the I are placed within the meadow word

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports spotting a female bird in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a woman's given name, so it fits a clue asking for a female.

clue.text: Copper had dandy stopped from travelling

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a toff is a smartly dressed upper-class man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A policeman detained a fop and prevented him from going on his journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut off is isolated, prevented from reaching or leaving a place.

clue.text: Customers have legal right to telephone accepted by engineer

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the other pieces go inside the engineer's letters

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Buyers are entitled to have an engineer take their phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A clientele is the body of customers a business serves, a collective synonym.

clue.text: Peg gets to fall heavily after losing footing

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot is the bottom, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: rain is said to teem when it falls heavily

explanation.surface: A tent peg is driven in after someone slips in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing footing' drops the last letter, the bottom of a down entry, from TEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf tee is a small peg on which the ball is set before driving.

clue.text: Like tights worn by a woman that may be out for a catch?

definitions.text: Like tights worn by a woman
definitions.meaning: describes open-mesh hosiery with a diamond weave

definitions.text: that may be out for a catch?
definitions.meaning: a mesh used by a fisherman to land his catch

explanation.definitionFit: Fishnet is both a style of open-weave stockings and literally the mesh that trawlers use.

clue.text: Flippancy about value of this flying certificate?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the flippancy word goes round the value word

parts.note: airiness is a light, flippant manner
worth means value

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the worth of a pilot's licence in a casual tone.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's certificate of airworthiness confirms its fitness to fly, so the quality is what the document certifies.

clue.text: Society needs one time to be abstemious and quiet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Lent is the Christian season of fasting and self-denial

explanation.surface: A club needs one season of self-restraint and calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Silent means making no sound, a synonym for quiet.

clue.text: Dancing with beat fading away

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
going means disappearing or fading away

explanation.surface: Ballroom dancers move to a rhythm that slowly dies away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' suggests rhythm in the dancing picture but means thrash, TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangoing is performing the tango, so it is a particular kind of dancing.

clue.text: Ordain tooth to be straightened? Yes, if you're concerned with this

definitions.text: Ordain tooth to be straightened? Yes, if you're concerned with this

indicators.note: being straightened means the letters of the two words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A dentist decrees that a crooked tooth must be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be straightened' makes an anagram of ORDAIN TOOTH; the whole clue then describes the specialism that straightens teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodontia is the dental branch that corrects irregular teeth, exactly what concerns a straightened tooth.

clue.text: Ready to work, learner gets facility for study leave

indicators.note: to work suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
facility can mean ease, effortlessness

explanation.surface: A trainee who is keen to start gets a grant for time off to study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' makes an anagram of READY, giving DAYRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Day release is a British scheme letting employees attend college one day a week, a form of study leave.

clue.text: Fateful few English went out flying, against them?

definitions.text: Fateful few English went out flying, against them?

indicators.note: went out says one letter leaves the mixed letters
flying suggests the letters are tossed into the air and rearranged

explanation.surface: The Few, Britain's fighter pilots in 1940, took off against the German air force.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from FATEFUL FEW ('went out') and rearrange the rest ('flying'). The Few are the RAF pilots of the Battle of Britain, who flew against the German air force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luftwaffe was the German air force that the RAF's Few fought in 1940.

clue.text: Repeated thanks given for so long

indicators.note: Repeated says the word for thanks is given twice

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Saying thanks twice over as a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a British informal goodbye, equivalent to so long.

clue.text: Rod in a foot of earth

definitions.meaning: a roasting rod pushed through meat over a fire
a spade's depth of soil, roughly a foot

explanation.definitionFit: A spit is both a skewer for roasting and a gardener's measure of a spade-blade depth of earth.

clue.text: Quiet man at the helm — one making earnest entreaty

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a leader is the person in charge, at the helm

explanation.surface: A silent captain steers the ship while someone begs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleader is one who pleads, making a heartfelt appeal or entreaty.

clue.text: Things swallowed outside a London college, hot stories

indicators.note: outside says the foods word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: foods are things swallowed
LSE is the London School of Economics
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Lies told at a London college are hot gossip that people swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' hints at gullibly believing lies, which suits the definition, but here it simply means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories, in the sense of fibs, are falsehoods.

clue.text: Merciful man that is associated with part of Bible

parts.note: Len is a man's name, short for Leonard
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A forgiving man is linked to a section of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means showing mercy or tolerance, a synonym of merciful.

clue.text: Port with lots of sand and lots of noise

parts.note: a dune is a heap of sand
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A harbour town on a sandy coast that is very noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a harbour city on New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Quiet success by German, the composer

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A German's understated triumph over a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American composer of Rhapsody in Blue.

clue.text: Soil crushed into small particles

definitions.meaning: past participle of grind, as with coffee

explanation.definitionFit: Ground means both earth or soil and something milled into a powder.

clue.text: One destined to enter grave without prayer?

definitions.text: One destined to enter grave without prayer?

parts.words: One destined to enter grave without prayer?
parts.note: someone doomed, who does not have a prayer of surviving and will soon be in the grave

explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone who is doomed or as good as dead, beyond hope.

clue.text: Like some coffee that's affected Diane badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are rearranged wrongly

explanation.surface: Coffee has upset Diane's system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes an anagram of AFFECTED DIANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Decaffeinated coffee has had its caffeine removed, a description of some coffee.

clue.text: Firm acquires good little piece of machinery

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company buys a fine small machine part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cog is a toothed wheel or tooth, a small component in machinery.

clue.text: Accent of Belfast's foremost conman

indicators.note: foremost takes the leading letter of the word Belfast

parts.note: a rogue is a dishonest swindler, a conman

explanation.surface: The leading confidence trickster in Belfast has a strong accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish.

clue.text: Areas of land getting only half of winter precipitation

indicators.note: only half of keeps just the second half of the word winter

parts.note: rains are falls of precipitation

explanation.surface: Fields receive only half the usual winter rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half of' keeps TER, the back half of WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrains are tracts of land considered by their physical features.
